title: lookahead probe (log-only): which STK_XR_XD rows counted at L60-80 were announced after the rebalance date, and does excluding them change who qualifies / who is held

title: one-name robustness: dxpit with 601229.XSHG (上海银行) removed from the qualifier set before the cascade

why: type: robustness / n-small attribution. Family §4 [升级：601229 单名问题]: i-1 (Δobj -0.2484) and i-2 (Δobj -0.1642) BOTH pushed 601229 out of bfive for 7/12 months and both lost big, and 601229 is 29.8% of dxpit's price P&L — so it is open whether those rejections (and the cascade's 'half the persistence effect') are mechanism or one name. Either answer is wanted: NOT-ONE-NAME licenses reading i-1/i-2 as mechanism and the candidate VAL as evidence about a rule; ONE-NAME-DEPENDENT says a VAL would test a stock, not a strategy. ⚠ Hindsight by construction (601229 is chosen BECAUSE it was the top earner): this book is a diagnostic, never a candidate, and some drop is mechanical (best winner replaced by the next name) — the -0.05 band allows for that. DECISION RULE (declared before the number), evaluated in order vs dxpit 0.2630 / sharpe 2.02: (a) NOT-ONE-NAME if Δobj >= -0.05 AND sharpe >= 1.0; (b) ONE-NAME-DEPENDENT if Δobj <= -0.10 OR sharpe < 1.0 — flag on the family page that the candidate's VAL is weak evidence of mechanism; (c) else PARTIAL. Secondary readings, reported not voted: (i) RANK-MARGIN — if obj <= 0.1952 (u-e9-dxew basket), the top-5 rank's whole advantage over the basket was 601229; (ii) i-1/i-2 attribution — this Δobj as a fraction of i-1's -0.2484 and i-2's -0.1642 (arithmetic ratio, not a decomposition; they removed 601229 for 7 months, this removes it for 12). title: realizability at the book's own feasibility floor: 20-bar median money >= 4e6 applied to dxpit's qualifier set before the cascade, every qualifier's median logged per rebalance
hypothesis: On HS300 pe>0 dividend qualifiers the 1x feasibility floor (1e6 / 5 / 0.05 = 4e6 CNY/day) removes no name on any of the 12 rebalances, so the curve is bit-identical to dxpit.
why: type: realizability (exit gate requires realizability >= 2; unknown BLOCKS; family §4 [阻塞 exit gate]). A prior cannot substitute — 大小盘轮动's floor was inert, ETF溢价's took 8.44 -> 1.10. KEY PROPERTY that lets one run do the work of several: controlReport's qualifier set is PATH-INDEPENDENT (depends only on the date, never on holdings), so logging every qualifier's 20-bar median money each month makes in==out at ANY floor exactly computable from this one log — a floor that removes no qualifier in any month leaves the book's inputs, and hence its curve, identical. That is a deterministic measurement, not a projection. It also covers the u-e9-dxew basket book (same qualifier set, smaller positions: 1e6/~50/0.05 ≈ 4e5), so realizabilityScope may name both books if the log clears them. ⚠ Capital grows to ~1.41M by year end, so the end-of-year 1x floor is ~5.6e6 — read it off the same log. DECLARED SCORING RULE for R (before the number): R=1 if the 4e6 floor removes >=1 qualifier in >=1 month AND (sharpe < 1.0 OR Δobj <= -0.05 vs dxpit); R=2 if it binds but sharpe >= 1.0 and Δobj > -0.05, OR it is inert (max|Δcum| = 0 vs dxpit, LIQFLOOR in==out 12/12) but some name that enters bten has a median below 4e7 (10x) in some month; R=3 iff inert AND every bten name's median >= 4e7 in every month (same 10x-headroom rule as 银行股轮动 liq-cap). Also report, free from the log: the all-qualifier minimum per month, and for each of 4e7 / 2e8 / 1e9 which months and names it would remove — that is liq-2's precondition. CONTROL: if inert, curve must equal dxpit bit-for-bit (0.2630 / 2.02 / 14.61); absent LIQMIN/LIQFLOOR lines = instrumentation failure, not 'inert'. Cost ~ one dxpit run plus one get_price(count=20) call per month.
design: Reference book dxpit. New study/蓝筹分红持续性/build-liq.js modelled on study/银行股轮动/build-liq.js and study/大小盘轮动/build-liq.js (dxpit source + edits + OVERRIDE). (1) ONE asserted behavioural edit in main(), right after `df=controlReport(df, context.current_dt.date())`: `df=filter_liquidity_floor(context, df)  # liq-1: ONLY behavioural change vs dxpit` — filters DataFrame rows on df.code, order-preserving, reset_index(drop=True), LIQ_FLOOR = 4e6. title: capacity point: rerun liq-1 at the lowest declared high floor that liq-1's LIQMIN log shows actually removes a qualifier (ladder 2e8, then 1e9)
hypothesis: dxpit stays above the 1.0 gate with Δobj >= -0.05 at a floor that genuinely removes names, i.e. gate-passing capacity >= floor/4 CNY (2e8 -> ~¥50M, 1e9 -> ~¥250M).
why: type: realizability / capacity curve. Does NOT feed the R score (liq-1 settles R); it bounds capacity, which §4 needs to choose between dxpit and the u-e9-dxew basket before VAL and which integration needs. FLOORS DECLARED NOW, picked from liq-1's log by a fixed rule (not a sweep): ladder {2e8 = 50x initial-capital floor, 1e9 = 250x}. Run the LOWEST rung that removes >=1 qualifier in >=1 month per liq-1's LIQMIN. If neither rung removes anything, DO NOT RUN — record 'capacity >= ~¥250M, inert by log' (deterministic, path-independent qualifier set). If 2e8 removes names, 1e9 is not run (one run max). PRECONDITION: liq-1 done with R >= 2 (if R=1 at 1x, higher floors can only be worse — drop). DECISION RULE: CAPACITY-OK if sharpe >= 1.0 AND Δobj >= -0.05 vs dxpit => gate-passing capacity >= floor/4; CAPACITY-BOUND if sharpe < 1.0 => capacity < floor/4; between = degraded-but-passing, report both. Log empty months: a floor that pushes n_qual <= 10 triggers the L102 cash rule — a real capacity consequence, name it. ⚠ As in 大小盘轮动, the floor models a manager DECLINING unfillable names, not partial fills. Cost ~ one dxpit run, or zero if skipped.
design: Same builder as liq-1 with LIQ_FLOOR set to the chosen rung; nothing else differs. Same LIQMIN / LIQFLOOR / DXMON logs; LIQFLOOR ERROR must be 0.
